title: Cistern fill-rate problem
brief: Pipe A fills an empty tank in 12 hours working alone. Pipe B fills the same tank in 18 hours working alone. Pipe C, a drain, empties a full tank in 24 hours. All three are opened simultaneously on an empty tank and left running continuously. Compute the exact time required to fill the tank completely, expressed as hours and minutes, rounded to the nearest minute.
verify: Recompute the combined rate as 1/12 + 1/18 - 1/24 = 5/72 tank/hour, invert to get the exact fill time in hours, convert the fractional hour to minutes, and confirm the submitted answer matches this value to the nearest minute.

title: Sum-of-cubes induction proof
brief: Prove by mathematical induction that for every positive integer n, the identity 1^3 + 2^3 + 3^3 + ... + n^3 = (n(n+1)/2)^2 holds exactly. Your proof must state the base case explicitly, state the inductive hypothesis, and show the full algebraic derivation of the inductive step from k to k+1 without skipping any line of the expansion.
verify: Confirm the base case n=1 holds numerically (1 = 1^2), then independently expand (k(k+1)/2)^2 + (k+1)^3 and check it algebraically reduces to ((k+1)(k+2)/2)^2 with every intermediate term accounted for; any unjustified skip invalidates the proof.

title: Bank ledger exact balance
brief: A checking account starts at $1,240.50. Over one week the following transactions post in this order: deposit $326.10; card purchase -$89.99; rent payment -$450.00; paycheck deposit +$1,002.35; coffee -$15.00; refund +$44.44; car payment -$600.00; late fee -$35.00. Compute the exact ending balance to the cent after all eight transactions have posted.
verify: Independently add the starting balance and every listed transaction in cents to avoid rounding drift, and check the resulting total matches the submitted ending balance exactly to the cent.

title: Four-runner logic grid
brief: Four runners, Ada, Ben, Cleo, and Dan, finished a race in positions 1st through 4th, each wearing a different one of red, blue, green, yellow. Clues: Ada did not finish 1st and did not wear blue. The green-shirted runner finished immediately before Ben. Cleo finished 3rd. Dan wore red and finished 1st. The yellow-shirted runner finished 4th. Determine every runner's exact position and shirt color.
verify: Take the proposed position-and-color assignment and check it against each of the five clues in turn, confirming all positions and all colors are used exactly once; the assignment is correct only if every single clue holds simultaneously.

title: Recurrence closed-form derivation
brief: A sequence is defined recursively by a(1) = 3 and a(n) = 2*a(n-1) + 1 for every n > 1. Derive a closed-form expression for a(n) purely in terms of n (no recursion), show the derivation steps, and then use that closed form to compute the exact value of a(10).
verify: Plug the derived closed form back into the recurrence to confirm it satisfies a(n) = 2a(n-1)+1 identically and matches a(1)=3, then separately iterate the recurrence ten times by hand and check that value agrees exactly with the closed form's a(10).

title: Find the factorization error
brief: A student solving 2x^2 - 8x + 6 = 0 divided by 2 to get x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0, then wrote x^2 - 4x + 3 = (x-1)(x-2), concluding x = 1 or x = 2. Determine whether the factorization step is correct. If it is wrong, identify the exact incorrect step and state the true roots of the original equation.
verify: Expand (x-1)(x-2) and compare it term-by-term to x^2-4x+3 to confirm it does not match, then independently solve x^2-4x+3=0 via the quadratic formula or correct factoring to obtain the true roots and check them against the submitted correction.

title: Name Candidates Avoiding Trademark Clashes
brief: A startup needs a name for a new note-taking app. These names are already trademarked and must NOT appear, even as a substring: Notion, Evernote, Bear, Obsidian, Craft, Roam. Generate 6 original candidate names plus a one-clause rationale for each. List them numbered 1-6 with the rationale beside each name.
verify: An agent can lowercase each candidate and confirm none contains any of the six forbidden strings as a substring, then count exactly 6 numbered entries each followed by a rationale clause.

title: Reverse-Brainstorm Mitigations for a Checkout Flow
brief: Our checkout flow loses 40% of users between cart and payment. Using reverse brainstorming: first list 5 distinct ways the flow could actively sabotage a purchase (e.g. hide the total price), then invert each sabotage into a concrete design fix. Present as 5 paired rows: sabotage -> fix.
verify: An agent can parse the output for exactly 5 paired rows and confirm each fix row directly negates or reverses the specific sabotage stated immediately before it, rather than a generic checkout tip.

title: Forced Combination: Beekeeping x Supply Chain
brief: Force-combine two unrelated domains into one new product concept: beekeeping and supply-chain logistics. Name the concept, then write 4-6 sentences describing its mechanism, using at least one specific term from each domain (e.g. 'waggle dance', 'colony collapse' vs 'last-mile', 'just-in-time').
verify: An agent can lowercase the description and confirm it contains at least one term from the beekeeping glossary and at least one term from the supply-chain glossary provided in the brief.

title: Metaphor Set for Technical Debt, With Failure Points
brief: Generate 4 distinct metaphors for explaining 'technical debt' to a non-engineer, drawn from unrelated registers (cooking, geology, gardening, debt collection, or another of your choosing). For each metaphor, add a second sentence starting 'Breaks down when...' naming where the analogy misleads.
verify: An agent can confirm exactly 4 metaphor entries, each immediately followed by a sentence beginning 'Breaks down when', and that no two entries draw on the same source register.

title: Three Storage Schemas for the Same Post-Tagging Feature
brief: Requirement: users write posts and attach 1-20 free-text tags; the app must support 'find all posts sharing 3+ tags with post X'. Propose 3 alternative data-storage designs (e.g. relational join table, document store with tag arrays, graph store) for this feature. For each, name the paradigm and the one query it makes cheapest.
verify: An agent can check the response names 3 different storage paradigms with no repeats, and that each entry states a specific query it optimizes for, distinct from the other two.

title: Five Industries for Repurposing Sawdust
brief: A furniture workshop generates 200kg of fine sawdust waste weekly, currently landfilled. Brainstorm 5 concrete reuse applications for this sawdust, each in a DIFFERENT industry (e.g. not two food-industry ideas). For each, name the industry and describe the specific use in one sentence.
verify: An agent can extract the industry label from each of the 5 entries and confirm all 5 are distinct, with no repeated industry appearing across the list.

title: Locate First Mention of a Decision in Session Log
brief:
Search the following project session log for when the team first decided to switch database vendors:
[S12, 2026-01-04] Discussed latency issues with current provider.
[S15, 2026-01-11] Evaluated three alternative vendors.
[S19, 2026-01-20] Team voted to migrate to VendorX.
[S24, 2026-02-02] Migration to VendorX completed.
State the session ID, date, and exact entry text where the decision was first made, not where it was merely discussed or executed.
verify: The agent can grep the log for the earliest entry containing decision language (voted/decided) rather than discussion or execution language, and confirm the cited session ID, date, and quoted text match that entry exactly.

title: Count Breaking-Change Releases in Changelog
brief:
Review this changelog:
v2.0.0 (2025-06-01) [BREAKING] Removed legacy auth endpoint
v2.1.0 (2025-06-15) [FEATURE] Added rate limiting
v2.2.0 (2025-07-01) [BREAKING] Changed response schema for /users
v2.2.1 (2025-07-03) [FIX] Patched null pointer in schema validator
v3.0.0 (2025-08-01) [BREAKING] Dropped Python 2 support
Count how many releases are tagged BREAKING and list their version numbers in the final summary.
verify: The agent can write a script to count lines containing the literal tag [BREAKING] and check the reported count and version list against that tally.

title: Compute Longest Gap Between Logged Check-ins
brief:
Below are Priya's daily check-in timestamps from the team log:
2026-03-02 09:14
2026-03-03 09:20
2026-03-04 09:05
2026-03-09 09:30
2026-03-10 09:12
Recall the full check-in history and compute the longest gap, in days, between two consecutive check-ins. State which two dates bound that gap in the final summary.
verify: The agent can parse the timestamps in a script, compute all pairwise consecutive-day deltas, and confirm the maximum delta and its two bounding dates match the report.

title: Extract Verbatim Attribution Record from Transcript
brief:
Meeting transcript:
[00:02] Marcus: We should delay launch until QA finishes regression testing.
[00:05] Priya: Agreed, but send the customer email today.
[00:09] Marcus: Fine, I will draft it.
[00:14] Priya: I will review it by 3pm.
Convert this into a structured minutes record: one row per turn with timestamp, speaker, and the exact quoted statement (no paraphrasing), since this record becomes the citable source others will reference later.
verify: The agent can check that every timestamped turn from the source appears exactly once as a row, with speaker name, timestamp, and quoted text matching the transcript verbatim, character for character.

title: Match Support Ticket to Resolved Precedent
brief:
New ticket #4821: "App crashes on startup after updating to v5.2, Android 13 devices only."
Resolved ticket archive:
#3190 (Android, v4.8): crash on startup, stale cache key; fixed by cache-version bump.
#3502 (iOS, v5.0): crash on login, expired auth token; fixed by refresh-token retry.
#3877 (Android, v5.1): crash on startup on Android 13, permission API change; fixed by runtime permission check.
Identify the archived ticket that is the closest precedent for #4821, citing its ID and its original fix verbatim.
verify: The agent can confirm the cited ticket's platform, OS version, and symptom overlap with #4821 more closely than the other two archived tickets, and that the quoted fix text is copied verbatim from that ticket's record.

title: Rank Servers by Historical Incident Count
brief:
Incident log:
2026-01-03 node-07 disk full
2026-01-14 node-03 OOM kill
2026-02-02 node-07 disk full
2026-02-19 node-07 network timeout
2026-03-01 node-03 OOM kill
2026-03-15 node-11 disk full
Rank node-07, node-03, and node-11 from most to least past incidents recorded above, citing each server's total count in the final summary.
verify: The agent can tally occurrences of each server name in the log with a script and confirm the reported ranking order and each per-server count match that tally exactly.

title: Score Paragraph Readability
brief: Compute the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level for this paragraph: "Renewable energy adoption has accelerated across manufacturing sectors as production costs decline. Companies now weigh long-term maintenance savings against upfront capital expense when selecting equipment. Analysts expect the trend to continue if raw material prices stabilize." Show your sentence count, word count, and syllable count, then report the final grade-level number to one decimal place.
verify: Independently recount the sentences, words, and syllables in the source text and recompute the standard Flesch-Kincaid formula from scratch; the answer is correct only if the recomputed grade level matches the reported one within 0.2.

title: Rank Proverb Translations by Fidelity
brief: The French proverb "Petit a petit, l'oiseau fait son nid" has been rendered four ways: (A) "Little by little, the bird builds its nest." (B) "Bit by bit, the bird makes its home." (C) "Patience builds the nest." (D) "Slow and steady wins the race." Rank these four from most to least faithful to both the literal meaning and the idiomatic register of the original.
verify: Score each translation independently on two axes -- literal word-for-word correspondence and preservation of the proverb's incremental-progress meaning -- and check that the stated ranking is consistent with both axes combined, not just one.

title: Locate Ambiguous Pronoun References
brief: Number the sentences in this passage 1-4: (1) When Sarah handed the report to Priya, she thanked her for the quick turnaround. (2) The manager told the intern he would need to redo the slides. (3) The cat sat on the mat. (4) After the client called the vendor, they scheduled a follow-up. For each sentence, state whether a pronoun's antecedent is ambiguous, and if so, name the pronoun and its two candidate antecedents.
verify: Re-read each sentence independently and check whether the flagged pronoun grammatically permits more than one antecedent; the answer is right only if every truly ambiguous case is flagged with correct candidates and unambiguous sentences (e.g. sentence 3) are not flagged.

title: Convert Citation to Chicago Author-Date
brief: Convert this APA-style reference into Chicago author-date style: Kwan, T. L., & Ibrahim, S. (2021). Semantic drift in loanword adaptation. Journal of Applied Linguistics, 44(3), 211-229. https://doi.org/10.1234/jal.2021.0044. Preserve all bibliographic facts but change author-name order, punctuation, and element order to match Chicago 17th edition author-date reference-list format exactly.
verify: Check the output field by field against the Chicago 17th edition author-date checklist -- author name order, year placement, title capitalization, italicized journal title, volume(issue), page range, and DOI -- confirming no field was dropped, invented, or left in APA order.

title: Identify Word-Formation Devices in Brand Names
brief: For each of these five product names, identify the word-formation device used (blend, clipping, acronym, compounding, or calque) and the source word(s) it derives from: "Instacart", "FedEx", "NASDAQ", "Netflix", "Wi-Fi". State the device and the decomposition for each name.
verify: For each name, check that recombining the claimed source morphemes actually reproduces the name's spelling or sound, and that the labeled device matches its standard linguistic definition (e.g. a blend fuses word fragments, an acronym is pronounced letter-by-letter).

title: Judge Paraphrase Fidelity
brief: Original sentence: "Even the interns understood the new policy." Paraphrase A: "The interns, like everyone else, understood the new policy." Paraphrase B: "The interns understood the new policy, unlike everyone else." Decide which paraphrase preserves the original's implication that the policy was easy to understand, and explain what the other paraphrase incorrectly implies instead.
verify: Test each paraphrase against the original's scalar implicature (that interns, as a low-competence group, understood it) by checking entailment; the correct judgement names the paraphrase whose implicature matches and correctly identifies the reversed implicature in the other.

title: Derive Brier Score from Forecast Log
brief:
Review 5 past forecasts with stated confidence and actual outcomes:
1) conf 0.9, outcome: TRUE
2) conf 0.6, outcome: FALSE
3) conf 0.8, outcome: TRUE
4) conf 0.3, outcome: FALSE
5) conf 0.7, outcome: FALSE
Compute the Brier score for this forecaster and state whether it indicates good calibration (below 0.2 counts as well-calibrated). The final summary must show the computed score and the calibration verdict.
verify: The agent can recompute the mean squared error between each stated confidence and its outcome (1/0) in python3 and confirm the score matches and the threshold comparison is applied correctly.

title: Locate the Faulty Step in a Reasoning Chain
brief:
Review this solved chain for 'A train travels 60 miles in 1.5 hours; find its speed in mph':
Step 1: distance = 60 miles, time = 1.5 hours.
Step 2: speed = distance / time.
Step 3: speed = 60 / 1.5.
Step 4: speed = 30 mph.
Locate the exact step number where the result first diverges from the correct value, and give the correct value at that step. The final summary must name the step number and the corrected value.
verify: The agent can independently compute 60/1.5=40 in python3 and confirm the divergence is first introduced at step 4, not steps 1-3.

title: Rank Claims by Strength of Cited Evidence
brief:
Three claims were submitted with supporting evidence:
Claim A: 'Feature X improved retention' — evidence: one anecdotal user comment.
Claim B: 'Feature Y improved retention 12%' — evidence: A/B test, n=4,000, p=0.03.
Claim C: 'Feature Z improved retention' — evidence: internal team consensus, no data.
Rank the claims from most to least justified by their evidence and give a one-line rationale per claim. The final summary must present the ordered ranking with rationale.
verify: The agent can check the ranking places the statistically-tested claim (B) first and the no-data claim (C) last, matching a rubric that weights evidence type (test > anecdote > consensus-without-data).

title: Count Unsupported Assertions in a Status Report
brief:
Review this status report excerpt:
(1) Latency dropped 40% after the cache change [see dashboard]. (2) Users love the new onboarding flow. (3) Error rate is now near zero [see incident log, 2 errors/10k]. (4) The team is clearly more productive this sprint.
Count how many of the four numbered sentences assert a claim with no cited evidence attached. The final summary must state the count and list which sentence numbers lack support.
verify: The agent can parse each sentence in python3 for a bracketed citation marker and confirm the unsupported count is 2, corresponding to sentences 2 and 4.

title: Decide Whether to Escalate a Low-Confidence Answer
brief: An agent answered a medication-dosage question with self-assessed confidence 0.42 out of 1.0, drawn from conflicting sources. Policy: escalate to human review if confidence < 0.7 OR the topic involves dosage/safety. Apply the policy to this case and decide whether to answer as-is or escalate. The final summary must state the decision and name which policy condition(s) triggered it.
verify: The agent can evaluate the policy as a boolean expression in python3 (confidence<0.7 OR is_safety_topic) against the given values and confirm the decision is 'escalate' with both conditions cited as triggers.

title: Rewrite Overconfident Claims to Match Evidence
brief: Rewrite this sentence so its confidence language matches the evidence actually available: 'This new algorithm is definitely faster than the old one in every case,' given the only evidence is a single benchmark run on one input size showing a 15% speedup. Produce a rewritten sentence using appropriately hedged, scoped language. The final summary must show the original sentence and the calibrated rewrite side by side.
verify: The agent can check the rewrite removes absolute terms ('definitely', 'every case'), restricts the claim to the single tested input size, and introduces no new unverified claims beyond the 15% figure given.

title: Deploy and Tear Down a Local Web Server
brief: Create a directory `site` with a file `site/index.html` containing exactly the string `OK-9231`. Start `python3 -m http.server 8790` from `site` in the background via run_shell, poll `curl -s localhost:8790` until it returns `OK-9231`, then terminate the server process and confirm port 8790 is no longer listening. The final summary must state the response body received and confirm the port was freed after shutdown.
verify: The agent can run `curl -s localhost:8790` to confirm the exact response body, then run `lsof -i :8790` (or equivalent) after shutdown to confirm nothing is listening.

title: Git Tag and Version Bump Workflow
brief: Initialize a git repo in `relx/`. Create `VERSION` containing `1.0.0`, commit it, then create an annotated tag `v1.0.0`. Bump `VERSION` to `1.1.0` and commit again. Run `git describe --tags` via run_shell. The final summary must state the exact tag created, the two commit messages used, and the literal output of `git describe --tags`.
verify: The agent can run `git describe --tags` and check the output matches the pattern `v1.0.0-1-g[0-9a-f]{7,}` for the current HEAD.

title: Resolve a Merge Conflict in a Config File
brief: On branch `main`, `settings.ini` contains `timeout=30`. On a new branch `feature/timeout`, change it to `timeout=90` and commit. Merge `feature/timeout` into `main` via run_shell; it will conflict on that line. Resolve the conflict by setting the final value to `timeout=60`, remove all conflict markers, and complete the merge commit. The final summary must state the resolved file's exact contents and confirm `git status` is clean.
verify: The agent can `cat settings.ini` to confirm it equals `timeout=60` with no `<<<<<<<`/`=======`/`>>>>>>>` markers, and run `git status --porcelain` to confirm empty output.

title: Rename a Function Across Three Modules
brief: Three files exist: `math_utils.py` (`def calc_total(items): return sum(items)`), `report.py` (`from math_utils import calc_total`), and `main.py` (`from report import calc_total\nprint(calc_total([1,2,3]))`). Using edit_file or sed, rename `calc_total` to `compute_total` in the definition and both call sites, then run `python3 main.py` via run_code. The final summary must state the stdout value, the exit code, and confirm zero remaining occurrences of the old name.
verify: The agent can run `grep -r calc_total .` and confirm zero matches, then run `python3 main.py` and confirm stdout is `6` with exit code 0.

title: Enforce Build Order in a Makefile Pipeline
brief: Write a `Makefile` with targets `fetch`, `transform` (depends on `fetch`), and `report` (depends on `transform`); each target appends its own name plus a timestamp to `build.log` before doing its work. Run `make report` once via run_shell. The final summary must list the exact target order recorded in `build.log` and confirm each target fired exactly once.
verify: The agent can `cat build.log` and confirm the three target names appear in the order fetch, transform, report with no duplicates.

title: Debug and Fix a Compiled Summation Binary
brief: Compile this buggy C source with gcc: `int sum(int *a,int n){int s=0;for(int i=1;i<=n;i++)s+=a[i];return s;}` plus a main that prints `sum` for input `[4,9,2,7]` (expected 22) and for `[1,1,1]` (expected 3). Run the binary via run_shell, observe the wrong outputs, fix the off-by-one loop bounds, recompile, and rerun both test cases. The final summary must state the buggy outputs, the fix applied, and the corrected outputs for both cases.
verify: The agent can recompile with gcc and run the binary against both input arrays, confirming outputs of exactly 22 and 3.

title: Find the Critical Path in a Launch Plan
brief: A launch plan has 5 tasks: A (3 days, no deps), B (5 days, depends on A), C (4 days, depends on A), D (2 days, depends on B and C), E (3 days, depends on D). Determine the critical path (sequence of tasks) and the minimum total project duration in days. The final summary must list the critical-path task sequence and the total duration.
verify: The agent can implement a forward/backward CPM pass in python3 to compute each task's earliest/latest start and confirm which tasks have zero slack, matching the stated critical path and duration.

title: Work Backward from a Hard Deadline
brief: A product must ship by 5:00 PM. Before shipping: QA sign-off takes 90 minutes, staging deploy takes 45 minutes (after QA), and a final smoke test takes 30 minutes (after deploy). Working backward from the 5:00 PM deadline, determine the latest clock time each of the three steps must start, and state whether starting QA right now at 1:30 PM is early enough. The final summary must give the three latest start times and a go/no-go verdict.
verify: The agent can subtract durations sequentially backward from 5:00 PM using python3 datetime arithmetic and compare the computed QA latest-start time against 1:30 PM.

title: Choose Between Two Deployment Strategies
brief: Compare two rollout plans for a risky config change. Canary rollout: costs $800 to run and has a 5% chance of a failure costing $12,000 in downtime. Big-bang rollout: costs $100 to run and has a 30% chance of the same $12,000 failure. Compute the expected total cost of each plan and recommend which to use. The final summary must state both expected costs and name the recommended plan.
verify: The agent can compute expected_cost = rollout_cost + failure_probability * failure_cost for each plan in python3 and confirm the recommendation matches whichever value is lower.

title: Forecast Battery Depletion Under Compounding Drain
brief: A drone battery starts at 100% charge. Each hour of flight in cold weather, the drain rate itself increases: hour 1 drains 8%, and each subsequent hour's drain rate is 15% higher than the previous hour's. Forecast the hour at which remaining charge first drops below the 20% abort threshold. The final summary must state the charge level at each hour and the abort hour.
verify: The agent can write a python3 loop applying the compounding drain rate hour by hour and confirm the first hour where remaining charge falls under 20% matches the stated abort hour.

title: Estimate SLA-Breach Probability from Latency Stats
brief: A request passes through 3 sequential services with independent processing times (mean, standard deviation in ms): Service A (40, 8), Service B (65, 12), Service C (25, 5). Using a normal approximation for the summed distribution, estimate the probability that total latency exceeds the 150ms SLA threshold. The final summary must state the combined mean, combined standard deviation, and the estimated exceedance probability.
verify: The agent can sum the means and variances analytically, compute a z-score, and check the exceedance probability via the normal CDF (e.g. statistics.NormalDist) in python3, without running a stochastic simulation loop.

title: Replan Downstream Dates After a Slipped Milestone
brief: A project schedule: Task1 starts Day 0, lasts 4 days. Task2 depends on Task1, lasts 3 days. Task3 depends on Task1, lasts 5 days. Task4 depends on both Task2 and Task3, lasts 2 days. Task1 slips by 3 days. Recompute the new start day for Task2, Task3, and Task4. The final summary must give each task's new start day after the slip propagates.
verify: The agent can re-run a forward-pass dependency scheduler in python3 taking the max finish time of each task's predecessors as its new start, and confirm each downstream start day shifted correctly given Task1's 3-day slip.

title: Count Exact Status-Code Matches in Log
verify: The agent can grep -c the exact literal substring "status":504 in the log block and confirm its reported integer equals that count (correct answer is 4).

title: Locate Field Offsets in Irregular Fixed-Width Rows
brief:
Read the following raw fixed-width employee report exactly as spaced, with no header row to anchor columns:
1001      Alice Chen     Engineering   95000
1002   Bo Martinez        Sales      61000
1003       Carla Diaz  Engineering      88000
For each row, report the zero-indexed character column at which the department name literally begins in that row's raw string. Do not re-align, pad, or assume the columns share a start position. The final summary must list one offset integer per row, in row order.
verify: The agent can run each raw row string through str.find() on the department substring in python3 and check the reported offsets match exactly, character for character.

title: Enumerate Line-Level Differences Between Two Configs
verify: The agent can run python's difflib.unified_diff over the two raw blocks and confirm the reported changed/added lines match the diff output exactly (one changed proxy_pass line, one added keepalive line).

title: Decode Literal Content of a Base64 Blob
brief:
The following string is base64-encoded raw text captured from a config file:
U2VydmVyOiBhcGktZ2F0ZXdheS0wMwpQb3J0OiA4NDQzClRMUzogZW5hYmxlZAo=
Decode it and report the exact literal plaintext it contains, character for character, with no correction of typos and no interpretation of what the fields mean. The final summary must give the decoded text verbatim, preserving line breaks.
verify: The agent can run base64.b64decode on the string in python3 and byte-compare the result against the reported decoded text.

title: Measure Exact Bar Widths in an ASCII Chart
brief:
Below is an ASCII bar chart of disk usage per volume, where each "#" represents raw character width, not a scaled unit:
/data  |##########################
/logs  |########
/tmp   |###
/cache |##################
Count the literal number of "#" characters in each bar exactly as printed. Do not infer a scale or convert to percentages. The final summary must list each volume name paired with its exact character count.
verify: The agent can count the '#' characters per line with python3 (str.count) and check the reported numbers match exactly (26, 8, 3, 18).

title: Partition Sensor Lines by Strict Format Compliance
brief:
Below are 6 raw sensor readings. A valid line matches exactly: two uppercase letters, three digits, a space, "VAL:", a number with exactly two decimal places, a space, "UNIT:", then C, F, or PA.
AB123 VAL:20.50 UNIT:C
ab124 VAL:21.00 UNIT:F
CD125 VAL:19.5 UNIT:C
EF126 VAL:88.00 UNIT:PA
GH127 VAL:15.00 UNIT:K
IJ128 VAL:30.25 UNIT:F
Sort each line, copied verbatim, into a valid group and an invalid group. Do not correct or guess intended values. The final summary must list both groups exactly as the lines above.
verify: The agent can apply the regex ^[A-Z]{2}\d{3} VAL:\d+\.\d{2} UNIT:(C|F|PA)$ with re.fullmatch to each line in python3 and confirm the reported valid/invalid partition matches (valid: lines 1,4,6; invalid: 2,3,5).

title: Tally Sentiment Across Customer Comments
brief:
Five customers left comments on a pricing change announcement:
1. "Finally, this makes sense for what I actually use."
2. "So my bill just doubles overnight? No warning?"
3. "Does this affect the annual plan too or just monthly?"
4. "This is exactly why I'm cancelling."
5. "Wish you'd given us more notice, but I get why you did it."
Classify each comment as satisfied, frustrated, confused, or mixed, then report totals per category.
verify: The agent can independently re-read each of the five comments, assign its own classification, and confirm both the per-comment labels and the category totals match, with counts summing to five.

title: Rank Support Tickets by Response Priority
brief:
Four tickets arrived within the hour:
A) A five-year customer, tone calm, reports a minor UI glitch.
B) A new trial user, tone sarcastic, says the product 'is a joke' after one crash.
C) A long-time enterprise contact, tone controlled but says 'this is the third outage this month, I'm losing patience.'
D) A first-time user, confused, asking how to reset a password.
Rank A-D in the order you would respond, and justify each rank in one line.
verify: The agent can check the output lists a full ordering of A, B, C, D with no repeats or omissions, and that the justification for the top rank explicitly cites relational stakes (tenure, repeated failures, or trust erosion) rather than ticket recency alone.

title: Infer a Vendor's Negotiating Leverage
brief: A vendor replies to your request for a 10% price cut: "We'd love to help, but our raw material costs rose 15% this quarter, and honestly, three other clients are already paying our new rate without complaint." Determine whether this reads as a genuine cost constraint or a negotiating tactic, state your confidence, and cite the specific phrases that support your read.
verify: The agent can check the answer states an explicit genuine-vs-tactic judgement, names a confidence level, and quotes at least two distinct phrases from the vendor's message as evidence, such as the unprompted comparison to other clients.

title: Soften Delivery of Performance Feedback
brief: A manager drafted this note to a report who has grown visibly defensive after recent critique: "You missed two deadlines, your code review comments are dismissive, and the client call went badly because you weren't prepared." Rewrite the note so it still names all three issues plainly enough to act on, but frames them in a way that won't trigger a defensive shutdown.
verify: The agent can check the rewrite still references all three original issues (deadlines, review comments, client call prep) and that blunt or accusatory phrasing like 'you failed' or 'unacceptable' has been replaced with framing that names impact and invites a next step.

title: Locate the Real Objection in a Client Renewal Email
brief: A client's renewal email reads: "We've reviewed the numbers and honestly the budget is tight this year, budget is always the first thing that gets cut. Also, not that it matters much now, but we were pretty caught off guard when the migration deadline slipped without a heads-up last quarter." Quote the sentence that reveals the client's real objection, and explain why it outweighs the stated reason.
verify: The agent can check the answer quotes the migration-deadline sentence verbatim from the source text (not the budget sentences) and explains that an unflagged broken commitment, not cost, is driving the hesitation.

title: Decide Whether to Escalate a Customer Threat
brief: Escalation policy: escalate if the customer mentions legal action, or if contract renewal is within 60 days and churn risk is raised. Situation: an enterprise customer, three years in, renewal in 25 days, writes: "After the third outage this month we've had our legal team review the SLA. We haven't decided anything yet, but we need this fixed." Decide escalate or not, and justify against the policy.
verify: The agent can check the decision is 'escalate', that the justification names both triggered conditions (legal mention, renewal within 60 days), and that it doesn't overstate the customer's claim as a decided lawsuit when the text says 'haven't decided anything yet.'

title: Locate the Disk Space Offender
brief: A project's disk usage report (du -sh --max-depth=1) shows these subdirectory sizes: cache 2.1G, logs 14.8G, models 3.4G, data 5.6G, tmp 0.3G, on a volume with 30G total capacity and 2.1G currently free. Identify the single subdirectory responsible for the overwhelming majority of consumed space and state its size and the percentage of total used space it represents.
verify: The agent can sum the listed sizes, compute each directory's share of total used space, and confirm the named directory's stated percentage independently against the raw numbers given.

title: Normalize Raw Telemetry into Health Codes
brief: Raw sensor readings: CPU temp 78C (WARN>=70, CRIT>=85), battery 14% (WARN<=20, CRIT<=5), fan RPM 0 (WARN if ==0), disk free 4% (WARN<=10, CRIT<=3), swap used 62% (WARN>=50, CRIT>=80). Apply the given thresholds to each reading and output a structured object mapping each metric name to exactly one status code: OK, WARN, or CRITICAL.
verify: The agent can independently apply each stated threshold rule to each raw value and check that the returned status code per metric matches exactly, with no metric omitted or mislabeled.

title: Build a Minimal Kill List to Free Memory
brief: Six running worker processes report resident memory: w1 512MB, w2 890MB, w3 210MB, w4 640MB, w5 1024MB, w6 305MB. The host must free at least 2048MB by terminating processes, killing the fewest possible. Rank candidates by memory footprint and output the ordered kill list (largest first) that meets the 2048MB target with the minimum process count.
verify: The agent can sort the listed processes by memory descending, sum the running total in that order, and confirm the returned list is the shortest prefix whose cumulative memory meets or exceeds 2048MB.

title: Diagnose a Leaking Process from Two Snapshots
brief: RSS memory sampled one hour apart for four processes: renderer 340MB->352MB, indexer 610MB->1180MB, cache-worker 220MB->238MB, logger 90MB->94MB. Compute each process's memory growth over the hour and identify which process is the leak candidate, reporting its name and its growth rate in MB per hour.
verify: The agent can subtract each process's before/after value, confirm the reported growth-rate arithmetic, and check that the named leak candidate is the one with the strictly largest computed delta.

title: Project Disk Exhaustion Time from Growth Trend
brief: This machine's free disk space was sampled at 4-hour intervals over one day: 08:00 - 210GB, 12:00 - 178GB, 16:00 - 146GB, 20:00 - 114GB. Assuming the trend continues linearly, derive the rate of space consumed per hour and calculate how many hours from the 20:00 reading until free space reaches zero.
verify: The agent can fit the four points to a line (or compute the consistent per-interval delta), recompute the hourly rate independently, and check the reported hours-to-zero against dividing 114GB by that rate.

title: Apply a Launch Health-Check Gate
brief: Before starting a new batch job, policy requires blocking launch if any metric exceeds 90% of its limit. Current readings: open file descriptors 950/1024, load average 7.8 on 8 cores, swap used 3.2GB of 4GB, GPU temperature 89C against a 95C limit. Decide GO or NO-GO for the launch and, if NO-GO, name the single metric that tripped the gate.
verify: The agent can compute each metric's percentage of its limit independently, confirm which (if any) exceed 90%, and check that the returned verdict and named trigger metric match that computation exactly.

title: Shortest Path Through Warehouse Maze
brief:
A warehouse floor is a 5x5 grid where '#' is a shelving wall, '.' is open floor, S is the forklift's start, and G is the loading dock:
S . # . .
. # . . .
. # . # .
. . . # G
# . . . .
Moving only up/down/left/right (no diagonals, never through '#'), find the shortest path from S to G. Report the path length in moves and the exact move sequence (e.g. D,R,U...).
verify: Re-run breadth-first search on the same grid to confirm the minimum move count, then step through the reported move sequence cell by cell to confirm each move stays in bounds, never crosses a '#', and ends exactly on G.

title: Count Building Wiring Clusters
brief: A building's ethernet wiring connects rooms as pairs: 1-2, 2-3, 4-5, 7-8, 8-9, 9-7. Rooms 6 and 10 have no wiring at all. Treating each pair as an undirected link, determine how many electrically separate wiring clusters exist across rooms 1 through 10, and list which rooms belong to each cluster.
verify: Build the undirected graph from the listed pairs and run union-find (or DFS) over all ten rooms; the cluster count and room memberships must match the reported groups exactly, including isolated single-room clusters.

title: Greedy Nearest-Neighbor Delivery Route
brief: A delivery drone starts at depot (0,0) and must visit waypoints A(3,4), B(6,1), C(1,7), D(8,8) via straight-line hops, always flying next to whichever unvisited waypoint is nearest in a straight line (greedy nearest-neighbor). Determine the visiting order and the total straight-line distance flown, rounded to two decimals.
verify: At each step recompute the Euclidean distance from the current point to every unvisited waypoint and confirm the nearest one was chosen next; independently sum the four hop distances and check the total matches the reported figure within 0.05.

title: Derive Tower Coordinates From Bearings
brief: Tower A sits at map origin (0,0) km. Tower B is 4km east and 3km north of Tower A. Tower C is 5km west and 2km south of Tower B. Tower D is 6km due north of Tower C. Derive the absolute (x, y) coordinates in km, relative to Tower A's origin, for Towers B, C, and D.
verify: Starting from A=(0,0), add each stated offset in sequence (east/west shifts x, north/south shifts y) and confirm the resulting coordinates; also subtract each pair of adjacent tower coordinates and check it reproduces the originally stated offset.

title: Crate-Through-Doorway Clearance Check
brief: A rigid crate measures 80cm wide by 190cm tall and cannot be tilted diagonally, only rotated 90 degrees flat. Three doorway openings (width x height) must be checked: Door 1: 90 x 200cm. Door 2: 75 x 185cm. Door 3: 190 x 85cm. For each doorway, decide whether the crate fits through in either orientation, and state which orientation (if any) works.
verify: For each door, test both orientations — (80,190) and (190,80) — against (door_width, door_height); a pass requires both crate dimensions to be less than or equal to the door's dimensions in that orientation. Confirm the reported yes/no and orientation match this test for all three doors.

title: Locate Optimal Distribution Hub
brief: Five warehouse facilities sit at (x,y) km coordinates: P1(0,0), P2(10,0), P3(10,10), P4(0,10), P5(5,5). Derive which single facility should host the central distribution hub, defined as the one minimizing the sum of straight-line distances to the other four facilities. Report the hub's ID and its total distance to the other four, rounded to two decimals.
verify: Independently compute, for every facility, the sum of Euclidean distances to the other four; confirm the reported hub corresponds to the minimum such sum and that the reported total matches the computed value within 0.05.

title: Count Escalation-Priority Accounts
brief: Given 6 customer accounts with (Monthly Revenue, Churn Risk Score 0-100): Acme:($8200,72) Borea:($1500,88) Cintel:($9400,45) Delve:($6100,81) Egress:($2300,30) Fenwick:($7700,66). An account qualifies as escalation-priority only if Monthly Revenue > $5000 AND Churn Risk Score > 60. Count how many accounts meet both conditions and name them. The final summary must state the count and list each qualifying account by name.
verify: The agent can recompute the compound threshold condition for each account in python and confirm the reported count and name list match exactly.

title: Identify Best-Value Marketing Channel
brief: Given 5 marketing channels with (Monthly Spend, Conversions, Avg Order Value): Search:($4000,80,$120) Social:($2500,50,$90) Affiliate:($1800,30,$150) Email:($300,40,$110) Display:($3200,45,$95). Value Score = (Conversions x Avg Order Value) / Monthly Spend. Identify the single channel with the highest Value Score only — do not produce a full ranking. The final summary must name that one channel and state its computed score.
verify: The agent can compute the Value Score for all 5 channels in python and confirm the named channel's score is strictly the maximum among them.

title: Allocate Quarterly Budget by Impact Score
brief: A $120,000 quarterly budget must be split across 4 initiatives in proportion to their stated Impact Scores, which sum to 100: Retention(40), Acquisition(25), Onboarding(20), Support Tooling(15). Calculate each initiative's dollar allocation as its proportional share of $120,000. The final summary must present a table of the 4 initiatives with exact dollar allocations that sum precisely to $120,000.
verify: The agent can recompute each allocation as (score/100)*120000 in python and confirm the four figures sum exactly to 120000.

title: Decide Go/No-Go on Vendor Contract Renewal
brief: A vendor contract renewal has a projected 3-year NPV of +$42,000 (favorable), but the vendor has missed 3 of the last 4 SLA deadlines and support tickets rose 60% this quarter. Weigh the favorable financial projection against the reliability trend and issue one go/no-go recommendation on renewal. The final summary must state the decision and explicitly address how the NPV figure and the SLA/ticket signal were weighed against each other.
verify: The agent can check that a single clear go/no-go verdict is present and that the reasoning explicitly references both the NPV figure and the reliability signal rather than resting on only one.

title: Test Robustness of Supplier Ranking to Cost Uncertainty
brief: 3 suppliers are ranked by Total Score = (Quality x 0.6) + (Reliability x 0.4) - (0.01 x UnitCost): SupplierX: Quality 90, Reliability 85, UnitCost $40 (known +/-$15 uncertainty). SupplierY: Quality 82, Reliability 95, UnitCost $22. SupplierZ: Quality 88, Reliability 80, UnitCost $30. Determine whether SupplierX's current #1 rank changes anywhere across its full UnitCost uncertainty range. The final summary must state the current top supplier, whether the ranking flips within the range, and the UnitCost value at which any flip occurs.
verify: The agent can recompute Total Score for all three suppliers at UnitCost=$25 and UnitCost=$55 (the range endpoints) in python and confirm the reported flip point and flip/no-flip conclusion match.

title: Consolidate Conflicting Stakeholder Priority Lists
brief: 3 stakeholders each ranked 4 launch features 1st-4th: Engineering: [Search, Notifications, Export, Themes]. Sales: [Export, Search, Themes, Notifications]. Support: [Notifications, Export, Search, Themes]. Using Borda count (1st=3pts, 2nd=2pts, 3rd=1pt, 4th=0pts, summed across stakeholders), produce one consolidated priority order, resolving any point ties by favoring the feature ranked higher by Engineering. The final summary must show each feature's total points and the final consolidated order.
verify: The agent can recompute Borda points for each feature from the three input lists in python, apply the stated tie-break rule, and confirm the consolidated order and point totals match exactly.
